## Summary

Brings a few missing previously UI-only `entire trail` features for trail collaboration metadata, approvals, and discussion threads.

### Metadata & approvals

- **`trail update`** — `--add/remove-assignee`, `--add/remove-reviewer`, `--type`, `--priority` (replace-set merge, mirroring `--add/remove-label`).

- Correctness fix: the server rejects a `body` update combined with any metadata field, so `runTrailUpdate` now splits body vs. metadata into separate PATCH calls (also fixes the interactive path, which previously sent status+title+body together). A partial-apply failure reports that the metadata change already landed.

### Discussion threads (`trail comment`)

`list` / `show <thread-id>` / `add [--title] -m` / `reply <thread-id> -m` / `edit <thread-id> <msg-id> -m` / `delete <thread-id> <msg-id> [-f]` / `resolve` / `unresolve`. Discussion-only by default (`--all` includes code-review threads, which are otherwise managed via `trail finding`).

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Assignees | ✅ update + create |
| Requested reviewers | ✅ update |
| Type (`bug\|feature\|task`) | ✅ update + create + show |
| Priority (`urgent\|high\|medium\|low\|none`) | ✅ update + create + show |
| Approvals (approve / request-changes / list) | ✅ |
| Discussion threads/comments | ✅ `trail comment` |
| Attachments | ⏭️ deferred |
| Watchers | ⏭️ deferred |

All new list/show commands provide `--json` and non-interactive fallbacks (agent-safe). Auth/not-logged-in messages go to stderr so `--json` stdout stays machine-parseable.

## Testing

- `mise run lint` — clean
- `mise run test` / `mise run test:integration` — pass
- Manual: `trail --help` and subtree `--help` show the new commands/flags.


The comment subtree helper `withNumberedTrail(cmd, ...)` *does* have `cmd`, so that one didn't need the change. But the approval helpers don't:

```go
func submitTrailApproval(ctx, w, errW, insecureHTTP bool, repoOverride, selector, branch, event, message, successVerb string) error

```

Their RunE already extracts the flag and passes `trailRepoFlag(cmd)` in as the `repoOverride` string — they never receive `cmd`. So to add the guard inside those helpers, I had two options:

1. Change the guard to take the `repoOverride` string it actually needs (one-line change at each of the 3 existing call sites: `ensureTrailRepoHasTarget(trailRepoFlag(cmd), …)`).
